choices.min_fwhm: one quarter of the narrowest component, to keep the search permissive

notes.reject_cancelling: True: a model with two overlapping components of opposite signs is refused (the reviewed engine refits it from the extrema of the data instead, reseed); on ERP CORE (40 participants x 7 components, real recordings) the LRP is within 10 ms of the published latency for 36 of 40 participants against 34 with the engine default, every other component unchanged; the engine default was measured on ECAP simulations, and on the layer-2 grid the two are within noise (CHANGELOG 'Second network run'; v1.1)
notes.component_labels: MMN (0.125-0.225), N2pc (0.200-0.275), LRP (-0.100-0.000) and ERN (0.000-0.100), all negative, added to the six labels of spec §6.1 (owner decision D6: REQ-274 names the seven ERP CORE components, the table labels three of them); the spec gives no number for these four, and §6.2 names the source of the erp windows, ERP CORE [LIT-erpmeas-39]: these are its published measurement windows, the ones of validation/erpcore.py and of benchmark task T6 (evoparam/benchmark/erpcore.json). They come after the six table labels, which keep their precedence where the windows overlap. LRP and ERN are measured on response-locked averages: the LRP window lies before the default fit window (from 50 ms), and in a stimulus-locked fit a negative component between 50 and 100 ms is named ERN, as one between 200 and 225 ms is named MMN; labels are names only (spec §5.5.7) (v1.2)
